desc: Parse input; build the graph of constraints (edges with X_i, Y_i, Z_i); immediately flag contradiction if any X_i == Y_i with Z_i != 0.
Compute connected components over vertices 1..N using a plain DSU over all edges (M up to 1e5), recording component sizes and member lists.

For each bit k in 0..29 (since Z_i ≤ 1e9 < 2^30), run a parity DSU (union-find with XOR weights) over the M edges using bit k of Z_i; if any union finds inconsistent parity, print -1 and exit. (Folded into single weighted DSU over full XOR values.)

For each component and each bit, determine the parity of each vertex relative to the component root from the parity DSU; count how many vertices would have bit 1 in the current orientation, and flip the component's bit if that count exceeds half the component size (minimizes ones per bit per component).
Accumulate A_v += (chosen bit) << k for every vertex and bit; isolated vertices stay 0.

Verify complexity O((N + M) * 30 α(N)) and memory O(N + M); output the resulting sequence (or all zeros when M=0), space-separated. (Single-DSU approach improves this to O((N+M) α(N)) plus O(30·N) for counting.)
Implement weighted DSU (parent, xor-diff array) with iterative find doing path compression while accumulating XOR.
Read input, process each constraint: union(X_i, Y_i, Z_i); on conflict print -1 and exit.
Group vertices by root via find; for each component compute size and per-bit counts of d[v].
Compute t per component from majority rule; assign A_v = t ⊕ d[v].
Fix early-exit token-consumption bug: loop always reads the three tokens per constraint and only performs union work while ok is true; verified against all three samples.
